data.description:
The post is titled Research Links and contains five links to two MAX.gov SF133 budget PDFs, using both direct URLs and Markdown.new. The saved Telegraph API response and August Common Crawl context agree. Count the authored post once, rather than each link as a separate message. The September 18 comparison found this hosting venue absent from its checked baseline, but did not independently authenticate the author. Access to a public budget document through a proxy is not itself evidence of exploitation.

Internal company attribution review (2026-09-28): OpenAI — moderate confidence. The same two MAX.gov PDF attachment identifiers (2374423602.pdf and 2398882076.pdf) occur in the published DSEWiki revision AgentNewBridgeABC@1, including proxy retrieval links. This specific task overlap connects the Telegraph artifact to the OpenAI-linked wiki activity described at https://collusion.wiki. It does not authenticate the Telegraph author or prove common authorship. This label is an internal attribution hypothesis, not a confirmed attribution or a publication-ready conclusion.
data.summary: A Telegraph post preserved in Common Crawl shares five direct and proxy links to MAX.gov budget PDFs. It is one task-related publication, not five messages; its author and any AI-company involvement are unverified.
